   157→```
   158→
   159→### Delete Flow (Soft-Delete)
   160→
   161→```
   162→User clicks "Delete" on file/folder
   163→  |
   164→  v
   165→[1] Remove item from parent folder's children array
   166→    (same as current: splice from children, publish updated folder metadata)
   167→  |
   168→  v
   169→[2] Create BinEntry from the removed FolderChild
   170→    - Copy FilePointer or FolderEntry
   171→    - Record originalParentIpnsName, originalPath, deletedAt
   172→    - Calculate size (for files: resolve file IPNS -> get size from FileMetadata)
   173→  |
   174→  v
   175→[3] Add BinEntry to RecycleBinMetadata.entries
   176→    Encrypt and publish bin IPNS record
   177→  |
   178→  v
   179→[4] DO NOT unpin CIDs (data stays on IPFS for recovery)
   180→    DO NOT unenroll from TEE republishing (IPNS records stay alive)
   181→  |
   182→  v
   183→[5] Update local stores:
   184→    - folderStore: remove item from parent children
   185→    - binStore: add new bin entry
   186→    - Search index: already excluded (not in folder tree)
   187→```
   188→
   189→### Restore Flow
   190→
   191→```
   192→User clicks "Restore" on bin item
   193→  |
   194→  v
   195→[1] Resolve originalParentIpnsName to find the target folder
   196→    - Walk folder tree to find folder with matching IPNS name
   197→    - If found: restore to that folder
   198→    - If NOT found: the parent was also deleted or moved
   199→      -> Check if parent is also in the bin
   200→      -> If parent in bin: recreate the folder path first (recursive restore)
   201→      -> If parent truly gone: restore to root folder
   202→  |
   203→  v
   204→[2] Add the preserved FolderChild back to the target folder's children
   205→    - For files: re-insert the FilePointer into parent's children array
   206→    - For folders: re-insert the FolderEntry into parent's children array
   207→    - Check for name collisions (append " (restored)" suffix if needed)
   208→  |
   209→  v
   210→[3] Publish updated parent folder metadata (IPNS)
   211→  |
   212→  v
   213→[4] Remove BinEntry from RecycleBinMetadata
   214→    Publish updated bin IPNS record
   215→  |
   216→  v
   217→[5] Update local stores:
   218→    - folderStore: add item back to parent children
   219→    - binStore: remove bin entry
   220→```
   221→
   222→### Permanent Delete Flow
   223→
   224→```
   225→User clicks "Delete permanently" or auto-purge triggers
   226→  |
   227→  v
   228→[1] For files:
   229→    - Resolve file's IPNS name -> get FileMetadata -> get CID(s)
   230→    - Unpin all CIDs (current version + past versions if any)
   231→    - Update quota (removeUsage)
   232→    - (TEE unenrollment deferred -- records expire naturally)
   233→  |
   234→  v
   235→[1b] For folders:
   236→    - Recursively resolve folder IPNS -> get all descendant file CIDs
   237→    - Unpin all CIDs
   238→    - Update quota
   239→  |
   240→  v
   241→[2] Remove BinEntry from RecycleBinMetadata
   242→    Publish updated bin IPNS record
   243→  |
   244→  v
   245→[3] Update local stores:
   246→    - binStore: remove entry
   247→    - quotaStore: adjust used bytes
   248→```
   249→
   250→### Auto-Purge Flow (Client-Side)
   251→
   252→```
   253→On app load OR when user navigates to /bin:
   254→  |
   255→  v
   256→[1] Load RecycleBinMetadata from IPNS
   257→  |
   258→  v
   259→[2] Filter entries where (now - deletedAt) > retentionPeriodMs
   260→  |
   261→  v
   262→[3] For each expired entry: execute permanent delete flow
   263→  |
   264→  v
   265→[4] Publish updated bin metadata (batch - single IPNS publish)
   266→```
   267→
   268→**Important**: Auto-purge is client-side only. If the user never opens the app, items remain in the bin past the retention period but are purged next time the client loads. This is acceptable because:
   269→
   270→- Storage quota still counts bin items (no free ride by not opening the app)
   271→- The retention period is a UX guideline, not a strict SLA
   272→- Server-side purge would require the server to decrypt bin metadata, violating zero-knowledge
   273→
   274→### Desktop FUSE Integration
   275→
   276→Current `handle_unlink` and `handle_rmdir` in `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/fuse/write_ops.rs`:
   277→
   278→1. Remove inode from local tree
   279→2. Update folder metadata (publish to IPNS)
   280→3. Fire-and-forget unpin of CID
   281→
   282→**Change**: Instead of unpinning in step 3, send a message to the webview to execute the soft-delete bin service call. The webview has the user's keys and can encrypt/publish the bin metadata.
   283→
   284→```
   285→Current FUSE unlink:
   286→  remove inode -> update folder IPNS -> unpin CID (fire-and-forget)
   287→
   288→New FUSE unlink:
   289→  remove inode -> update folder IPNS -> IPC to webview: "addToBin(item)"
   290→```
   291→
   292→The Rust side already sends metadata to the webview for IPNS publishing via `update_folder_metadata()`. The bin entry creation requires the user's ECIES public key for bin metadata encryption. This key is available in the webview's auth store. So the bin metadata publish must happen on the webview side.
   293→
   294→**Minimal approach**: The Rust `handle_unlink`/`handle_rmdir` already correctly removes the child from folder metadata and publishes. The only change needed is: instead of calling `unpin_content()`, emit a Tauri event or invoke a webview JS function that calls the bin service to add the entry. The item data (FilePointer/FolderEntry) needs to be captured before removal and passed to the webview.
   295→
   296→### Sync Across Devices
   297→
   298→The bin IPNS record is included in the same IPNS polling mechanism as folder metadata:
   299→
   300→- TEE republishes the bin IPNS record every 3 hours (enrolled on first bin write)
   301→- Client polls every 30s, compares bin IPNS CID
   302→- On change, re-fetches and decrypts bin metadata
   303→- Local bin store is updated
   304→
   305→**Conflict handling**: The bin metadata uses a `sequenceNumber` (same as DeviceRegistry). On concurrent modification, the conflict detection from Phase 16 applies. Use optimistic concurrency: if sequence mismatch on publish, re-read remote, merge entries, retry.
   306→
   307→**Merge strategy for bin entries**: Additive merge (union of entries). If both devices deleted different items simultaneously, the merged bin has both. If the same item appears in both (same bin entry ID), keep the one with the earlier `deletedAt` (or either -- they are identical since the same item was deleted).
   308→
   309→## Don't Hand-Roll
   310→
   311→| Problem                     | Don't Build           | Use Instead                                                                           | Why                                                              |
   312→| --------------------------- | --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
   313→| IPNS key derivation for bin | Custom key generation | HKDF with `cipherbox-recycle-bin-ipns-v1` info string, same pattern as vault/registry | Domain-separated, deterministic, established pattern             |
   314→| Bin metadata encryption     | Custom scheme         | ECIES with user's publicKey (same as DeviceRegistry)                                  | Zero-knowledge, user-scoped, no symmetric key to manage          |
   315→| Flat list UI                | Custom file browser   | Adapt existing `FileListItem` component pattern                                       | Consistent UX, reuse selection/context menu logic                |
   316→| Confirmation dialogs        | New dialog component  | Existing `ConfirmDialog` component                                                    | Already supports destructive styling, loading state              |
   317→| Multi-select                | Custom selection      | Existing `SelectionActionBar` pattern from FileBrowser                                | Consistent interaction, already supports batch operations        |
   318→| Auto-purge scheduling       | Server-side cron      | Client-side check on load/navigate                                                    | Zero-knowledge constraint -- server cannot read bin metadata     |
   319→| Environment config          | Hardcoded values      | NestJS `ConfigService` with `RECYCLE_BIN_RETENTION_DAYS`                              | Follows existing pattern (Redis, DB, CORS all use ConfigService) |
   320→
   321→**Key insight:** Every infrastructure piece needed for the recycle bin already exists in CipherBox. The bin is essentially a "special folder" with ECIES encryption (like device registry) instead of AES-GCM encryption (like regular folders), plus business logic for retention and restore.
   322→
   323→## Common Pitfalls
   324→
   325→### Pitfall 1: Orphaned IPNS Records Accumulating
   326→
   327→**What goes wrong:** Every deleted item's IPNS record remains enrolled in TEE republishing. If a user deletes hundreds of files and never permanently deletes them, the TEE republish queue grows indefinitely.
   328→**Why it happens:** Soft-delete intentionally keeps IPNS records alive for restore.
   329→**How to avoid:** On permanent delete, add TEE unenrollment (if an API endpoint exists by then -- currently deferred to "Phase 14 TODO"). At minimum, document this as a known limitation. The republish service already has capacity warnings at 1000+ records.
   330→**Warning signs:** TEE republish queue depth metric growing without plateau.
   331→
   332→### Pitfall 2: Bin Metadata Blob Size Growth
   333→
   334→**What goes wrong:** If a user deletes hundreds of items, each BinEntry contains a full FolderEntry or FilePointer. The bin metadata blob grows, increasing IPFS upload/download time.
   335→**Why it happens:** Each BinEntry preserves the full FolderChild for restore.
   336→**How to avoid:**
   337→
   338→- Auto-purge on load keeps the bin bounded by retention period
   339→- A 30-day retention with typical usage (say 100 items deleted per month) results in ~50KB of bin metadata. This is well within acceptable limits.
   340→- Add a safety check: if bin metadata exceeds 1MB, warn the user and suggest emptying the bin.
   341→  **Warning signs:** Bin load time > 2s.
   342→
   343→### Pitfall 3: Stale `originalParentIpnsName` After Folder Moves
   344→
   345→**What goes wrong:** User deletes a file from folder A, then moves folder A to a different location. The bin entry's `originalParentIpnsName` still points to folder A's IPNS name, which is correct (IPNS names don't change on move). But the `originalPath` display string is now inaccurate.
   346→**Why it happens:** The display path is captured at deletion time.
   347→**How to avoid:** Accept that `originalPath` is "path at deletion time" -- display it with a note "(at time of deletion)". The IPNS-based restore logic will correctly find the moved folder regardless of its current location in the tree.
   348→**Warning signs:** User confusion when displayed path doesn't match current folder structure.
   349→
   350→### Pitfall 4: Concurrent Delete-and-Restore Race
   351→
   352→**What goes wrong:** On device A, user deletes a file. On device B (before sync), user tries to access the same file. After sync, device B sees the file is gone.
   353→**Why it happens:** IPNS polling is 30s. Within that window, the two devices have divergent state.
   354→**How to avoid:** This is the same eventual consistency the app already handles for all operations. The sync mechanism (Phase 16) already handles concurrent modifications. The bin just adds a recovery path -- the user can restore the file from the bin on any device.
   355→**Warning signs:** None specific -- this is inherent to eventual consistency.
   356→
   357→### Pitfall 5: Deleting Shared Items
   358→
   359→**What goes wrong:** User deletes a file that is actively shared with another user. The file goes to the owner's bin, but the recipient loses access.
   360→**Why it happens:** The share references the item by IPNS name. When removed from the folder, the share's reference becomes dangling.
   361→**How to avoid:** For v1, accept this behavior -- the owner's delete takes precedence. The shared user will see a resolution error for that IPNS name. Future enhancement: notify shared users when a shared item is deleted.
   362→**Warning signs:** Share recipients see "file not found" errors.
   363→
   364→### Pitfall 6: Restoring to a Deleted Parent Folder
   365→
   366→**What goes wrong:** User deletes folder A (which contained file B), then tries to restore file B. The original parent (folder A) no longer exists in the folder tree.
   367→**Why it happens:** File B's `originalParentIpnsName` points to folder A, which is itself in the bin.
   368→**How to avoid:** Implement the "recreate path" logic from CONTEXT.md:
   369→
   370→1. Look up `originalParentIpnsName` in the folder tree
   371→2. If not found, check if a bin entry exists with a matching IPNS name
   372→3. If parent is in bin, restore the parent first (recursively)
   373→4. If parent is nowhere (permanently deleted), restore to root
   374→   This must be clearly implemented with recursion guards (max depth) to prevent infinite loops.
   375→   **Warning signs:** "Folder not found" errors during restore.
   376→
   377→### Pitfall 7: Size Calculation for Folder Bin Entries
   378→
   379→**What goes wrong:** When deleting a folder, its `size` for quota display and purge-time unpin requires resolving all descendant file metadata IPNS records. This is expensive.
   380→**Why it happens:** Folder metadata only contains FilePointers (no inline size), and the folder tree may have deep nesting.
   381→**How to avoid:**
   382→
   383→- On delete: if the folder's subtree is loaded in the folder store, calculate size from loaded data. If not fully loaded, use 0 as size and display "Unknown" in the bin.
   384→- On permanent delete: resolve the full subtree to unpin all CIDs. This is inherently async and can be done in background.
   385→- Accept that folder size in the bin view may be approximate or unknown.
   386→  **Warning signs:** Long delays during folder deletion if trying to resolve all descendant sizes eagerly.
   387→
   388→## Code Examples
   389→
   390→### Bin IPNS Key Derivation (follows registry pattern exactly)
   391→
   392→```typescript
   393→// Source: modeled on packages/crypto/src/registry/derive-ipns.ts
   394→const BIN_HKDF_SALT = new TextEncoder().encode('CipherBox-v1');
   395→const BIN_HKDF_INFO = new TextEncoder().encode('cipherbox-recycle-bin-ipns-v1');
   396→
   397→export async function deriveBinIpnsKeypair(userPrivateKey: Uint8Array): Promise<{
   398→  privateKey: Uint8Array;
   399→  publicKey: Uint8Array;
   400→  ipnsName: string;
   401→}> {
   402→  if (userPrivateKey.length !== SECP256K1_PRIVATE_KEY_SIZE) {
   403→    throw new CryptoError('Invalid private key size for bin derivation', 'INVALID_KEY_SIZE');
   404→  }
   405→
   406→  const ed25519Seed = await deriveKey({
   407→    inputKey: userPrivateKey,
   408→    salt: BIN_HKDF_SALT,
   409→    info: BIN_HKDF_INFO,
   410→    outputLength: 32,
   411→  });
   412→
   413→  const ed25519PublicKey = await ed.getPublicKeyAsync(ed25519Seed);
   414→  const ipnsName = await deriveIpnsName(ed25519PublicKey);
   415→
   416→  return { privateKey: ed25519Seed, publicKey: ed25519PublicKey, ipnsName };
   417→}
   418→```
   419→
   420→### Bin Metadata Encryption/Decryption (follows registry pattern)
   421→
   422→```typescript
   423→// Source: modeled on packages/crypto/src/registry/index.ts
   424→export async function encryptBinMetadata(
   425→  metadata: RecycleBinMetadata,
   426→  userPublicKey: Uint8Array
   427→): Promise<Uint8Array> {
   428→  const json = JSON.stringify(metadata);
   429→  const plaintext = new TextEncoder().encode(json);
   430→  return wrapKey(plaintext, userPublicKey); // ECIES encrypt
   431→}
   432→
   433→export async function decryptBinMetadata(
   434→  ciphertext: Uint8Array,
   435→  userPrivateKey: Uint8Array
   436→): Promise<RecycleBinMetadata> {
   437→  const plaintext = await unwrapKey(ciphertext, userPrivateKey);
   438→  const json = new TextDecoder().decode(plaintext);
   439→  return validateBinMetadata(JSON.parse(json));
   440→}
   441→```
   442→
   443→**Note:** The `wrapKey`/`unwrapKey` in CipherBox is ECIES encrypt/decrypt, not just symmetric key wrapping. It works on arbitrary-length plaintext (the ECIES implementation handles the internal AES encryption). This is confirmed by the DeviceRegistry pattern which encrypts the entire registry JSON blob via ECIES.
   444→
   445→### Bin Store (Zustand)
   446→
   447→```typescript
   448→// Source: modeled on stores/sync.store.ts and stores/share.store.ts
   449→type BinState = {
   450→  entries: BinEntry[];
   451→  isLoading: boolean;
   452→  isLoaded: boolean;
   453→  error: string | null;
   454→  sequenceNumber: number;
   455→  binIpnsName: string | null;
   456→
   457→  setEntries: (entries: BinEntry[], seq: number) => void;
   458→  addEntry: (entry: BinEntry) => void;
   459→  removeEntry: (entryId: string) => void;
   460→  removeEntries: (entryIds: string[]) => void;
   461→  setLoading: (loading: boolean) => void;
   462→  setError: (error: string | null) => void;
   463→  setBinIpnsName: (name: string) => void;
   464→  clearBin: () => void;
   465→};
   466→```
   467→
   468→### Soft-Delete in Folder Mutations (modified handleDelete)
   469→
   470→```typescript
   471→// In useFolderMutations.ts handleDelete, REPLACE the unpin fire-and-forget with:
   472→
   473→// Instead of:
   474→//   resolveIpnsRecord(ipnsName).then(r => unpinFromIpfs(r.cid))
   475→// Do:
   476→//   await binService.addToBin({ item, parentIpnsName, parentPath })
   477→
   478→// The bin service handles:
   479→// 1. Creating the BinEntry from the removed FolderChild
   480→// 2. Loading current bin metadata
   481→// 3. Appending the entry
   482→// 4. Encrypting and publishing the updated bin IPNS record
   483→```
   484→
   485→### Sidebar Addition
   486→
   487→```tsx
   488→// In AppSidebar.tsx, add between "Shared" and "Settings":
   489→<NavItem to="/bin" icon="bin" label="Bin" active={location.pathname.startsWith('/bin')} />
   490→```
   491→
   492→### Retention Configuration (API side)
   493→
   494→```typescript
   495→// In vault.service.ts or a new config endpoint
   496→const RECYCLE_BIN_RETENTION_DAYS = this.configService.get<number>(
   497→  'RECYCLE_BIN_RETENTION_DAYS',
   498→  30 // default 30 days for production
   499→);
   500→
   501→// Exposed to client via vault config or a new /config endpoint
   502→// Client reads this on login and stores in auth/vault store
   503→```
   504→
   505→```
   506→# .env.example
   507→RECYCLE_BIN_RETENTION_DAYS=30
   508→
   509→# .env (staging)
   510→RECYCLE_BIN_RETENTION_DAYS=2
   511→```
   512→
   513→### Client-Side Retention Constant
   514→
   515→```typescript
   516→// The retention period (in ms) comes from the API config response
   517→// Stored in vault store or a dedicated config store
   518→const RETENTION_MS = retentionDays * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;
   519→
   520→function isExpired(entry: BinEntry): boolean {
   521→  return Date.now() - entry.deletedAt > RETENTION_MS;
   522→}
   523→
   524→function daysRemaining(entry: BinEntry): number {
   525→  const elapsed = Date.now() - entry.deletedAt;
   526→  const remaining = RETENTION_MS - elapsed;
   527→  return Math.max(0, Math.ceil(remaining / (24 * 60 * 60 * 1000)));
   528→}
   529→```
   530→
   531→## State of the Art
   532→
   533→| Old Approach (before this phase)     | New Approach (this phase)                   | Impact                                     |
   534→| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
   535→| Delete = immediate unpin + permanent | Delete = soft-delete to bin, deferred unpin | Items are recoverable for retention period |
   536→| No bin metadata IPNS                 | HKDF-derived bin IPNS record                | Cross-device bin sync                      |
   537→| FUSE unlink = permanent              | FUSE unlink = soft-delete                   | Desktop deletions are recoverable from web |
   538→| Quota freed on delete                | Quota freed on permanent delete only        | Bin items count against quota              |
   539→
   540→**Deprecated/outdated:**
   541→
   542→- The current `deleteFile()` in `delete.service.ts` that directly unpins will be replaced by a soft-delete path. The `unpinFromIpfs` call moves to the permanent delete flow.
   543→
   544→## Open Questions
   545→
   546→1. **ECIES max plaintext size for bin metadata**
   547→   - What we know: DeviceRegistry uses ECIES for the entire blob. The eciesjs library uses AES-256-GCM internally for the payload, so there's no practical size limit.
   548→   - What's unclear: Performance with very large bin metadata (1000+ entries). Each entry is ~500 bytes, so 1000 entries = ~500KB ECIES payload.
   549→   - Recommendation: Test with 1000 entries during implementation. Add a safety cap (e.g., 5000 entries max) with a warning to empty the bin.
   550→
   551→2. **TEE enrollment for the bin IPNS record**
   552→   - What we know: TEE republishing keeps IPNS records alive. The bin IPNS record needs to be enrolled (same as vault, device registry, all folder IPNS records).
   553→   - What's unclear: The bin IPNS key is derived via HKDF, not randomly generated. Is the TEE enrollment path the same? (Answer: yes, the TEE receives the encrypted IPNS private key regardless of derivation method.)
   554→   - Recommendation: Enroll the bin IPNS key with TEE on first bin write, same as vault/registry IPNS enrollment.
   555→
   556→3. **Folder size in bin entries**
   557→   - What we know: Files have `size` in their FileMetadata. Folders don't have a single size -- need to sum all descendant files.
   558→   - What's unclear: How to handle partially-loaded folder trees (not all subfolders are loaded in memory).
   559→   - Recommendation: For files, use the known size from FileMetadata (resolved at delete time if possible). For folders, store 0 and display "Folder" without size. Size is only critical for quota (which is tracked server-side via pins anyway).
   560→
   561→4. **Batch operations and IPNS publish count**
   562→   - What we know: Deleting multiple items from the same folder = 1 folder IPNS publish + 1 bin IPNS publish.
   563→   - What's unclear: With optimistic concurrency, if the bin publish conflicts, the folder publish already succeeded. Need atomic-like behavior.
   564→   - Recommendation: Use add-before-remove pattern: write to bin first, then remove from folder. If bin publish fails, items stay in both places (recoverable). On next load, detect duplicates and reconcile.
   565→

   581→- `apps/web/src/components/file-browser/SelectionActionBar.tsx` -- Multi-select pattern
   582→- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/fuse/write_ops.rs` -- FUSE unlink/rmdir (lines 250-310, 547-610)

1→# Phase 17: Recycle Bin - Research
     2→
     3→**Researched:** 2026-03-04
     4→**Domain:** Client-side encrypted bin metadata, soft-delete flows, IPNS lifecycle management
     5→**Confidence:** HIGH
     6→
     7→## Summary
     8→
     9→The recycle bin feature introduces a soft-delete layer between the user's action (delete) and permanent data destruction (CID unpin). Instead of immediately unpinning CIDs and removing children from folder metadata, the delete flow will: (1) remove the item from its parent folder's metadata, (2) add a bin entry to a new encrypted bin IPNS record, and (3) defer CID unpinning until permanent delete or auto-purge.
    10→
    11→The architecture follows CipherBox's established zero-knowledge metadata pattern: a new IPNS record (the "bin index") encrypted with the user's public key via ECIES, deterministically discoverable via HKDF key derivation (same pattern as vault IPNS and device registry IPNS). Each bin entry preserves enough information to restore items to their original location. The bin IPNS record syncs across devices using the existing 30s IPNS polling mechanism.
    12→
    13→The implementation touches four layers: (1) the `@cipherbox/crypto` package (new bin metadata types and HKDF derivation), (2) web app services/stores/hooks/components (bin store, bin service, bin page, modified delete flows), (3) API backend (env-configurable retention constant, served to client), and (4) desktop FUSE (redirecting unlink/rmdir from permanent delete to soft-delete via webview IPC).
    14→
    15→**Primary recommendation:** Create a new `RecycleBinMetadata` IPNS record (ECIES-encrypted, HKDF-derived) that stores flat bin entries. Modify existing delete flows to write to the bin instead of unpinning. Add a `/bin` route with flat list view. Purge expired entries client-side on bin load.

    41→## Architecture Patterns
    42→
    43→### Bin Metadata IPNS Record
    44→
    45→A new IPNS record dedicated to the recycle bin, following the exact same pattern as the device registry:
    46→
    47→```
    48→Derivation:
    49→  secp256k1 privateKey (32 bytes)
    50→    -> HKDF-SHA256(salt="CipherBox-v1", info="cipherbox-recycle-bin-ipns-v1")
    51→    -> 32-byte Ed25519 seed
    52→    -> Ed25519 keypair
    53→    -> IPNS name (deterministic, discoverable from any device)
    54→
    55→Encryption: ECIES with user's secp256k1 publicKey
    56→Storage: IPFS blob, addressed via bin IPNS name
    57→```
    58→
    59→**Why ECIES instead of AES-GCM?** The device registry uses ECIES because there is no per-record symmetric key to manage. The bin metadata follows the same rationale -- it is a single user-scoped record, not a shared folder that needs per-folder keys. ECIES with the user's public key means only the user can decrypt it. This is the established pattern (see `packages/crypto/src/registry/derive-ipns.ts`).
    60→
    61→### RecycleBinMetadata Schema
    62→
    63→```typescript
    64→type RecycleBinMetadata = {
    65→  version: 'v1';
    66→  sequenceNumber: number; // Monotonically increasing, same pattern as DeviceRegistry
    67→  entries: BinEntry[];
    68→};
    69→
    70→type BinEntry = {
    71→  /** Unique ID for this bin entry */
    72→  id: string; // UUID
    73→  /** Original item type */
    74→  itemType: 'file' | 'folder';
    75→  /** Display name at time of deletion */
    76→  name: string;
    77→  /** IPNS name of the original parent folder (for restore path resolution) */
    78→  originalParentIpnsName: string;
    79→  /** Full breadcrumb path at deletion time (e.g., "My Vault / Documents / Reports") */
    80→  originalPath: string;
    81→  /** Unix timestamp (ms) when item was deleted */
    82→  deletedAt: number;
    83→  /** File/folder size in bytes (for quota display) */
    84→  size: number;
    85→  /** MIME type (files only, empty string for folders) */
    86→  mimeType: string;
    87→
    88→  // --- Item reference data (needed for restore and permanent delete) ---
    89→
    90→  /** For files: the FolderChild entry that was removed from parent metadata.
    91→   *  Stores the full FilePointer so restore can re-insert it. */
    92→  filePointer?: FilePointer;
    93→
    94→  /** For folders: the FolderChild entry that was removed from parent metadata.
    95→   *  Stores the full FolderEntry so restore can re-insert it. */
    96→  folderEntry?: FolderEntry;
    97→};
    98→```
    99→
   100→**Key design decisions:**
   101→
   102→1. **Store the full FolderChild entry**: When an item is deleted, its `FilePointer` or `FolderEntry` is preserved in the bin entry. This contains all ECIES-wrapped keys needed for restore (e.g., `folderKeyEncrypted`, `ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted`, `fileMetaIpnsName`). Without this, restore would be impossible since the keys are client-encrypted.
   103→
   104→2. **`originalParentIpnsName` instead of parent folder ID**: Folder IDs are internal to the in-memory tree. IPNS names are the stable, cross-device identifier (per Phase 16 merge logic). Using IPNS name enables restore even if the folder tree was rebuilt.
   105→
   106→3. **`originalPath` as display-only breadcrumb**: Stored at deletion time for UI display. Not used for restore logic (IPNS name is the authoritative reference).
   107→
   108→4. **File content CIDs are NOT unpinned on soft-delete**: The actual encrypted file data stays pinned on IPFS. Quota continues to count it. Only on permanent delete (manual or auto-purge) does CID unpinning occur.
   109→
   110→5. **Folder deletion stores only the top-level FolderEntry**: The folder's own IPNS record still exists on IPFS, so its children are preserved. Restore re-adds the FolderEntry to the parent. The folder's subtree is intact because we never unpinned or modified it.

   159→### Delete Flow (Soft-Delete)
   160→
   161→```
   162→User clicks "Delete" on file/folder
   163→  |
   164→  v
   165→[1] Remove item from parent folder's children array
   166→    (same as current: splice from children, publish updated folder metadata)
   167→  |
   168→  v
   169→[2] Create BinEntry from the removed FolderChild
   170→    - Copy FilePointer or FolderEntry
   171→    - Record originalParentIpnsName, originalPath, deletedAt
   172→    - Calculate size (for files: resolve file IPNS -> get size from FileMetadata)
   173→  |
   174→  v
   175→[3] Add BinEntry to RecycleBinMetadata.entries
   176→    Encrypt and publish bin IPNS record
   177→  |
   178→  v
   179→[4] DO NOT unpin CIDs (data stays on IPFS for recovery)
   180→    DO NOT unenroll from TEE republishing (IPNS records stay alive)
   181→  |
   182→  v
   183→[5] Update local stores:
   184→    - folderStore: remove item from parent children
   185→    - binStore: add new bin entry
   186→    - Search index: already excluded (not in folder tree)
   187→```
   188→
   189→### Restore Flow
   190→
   191→```
   192→User clicks "Restore" on bin item
   193→  |
   194→  v
   195→[1] Resolve originalParentIpnsName to find the target folder
   196→    - Walk folder tree to find folder with matching IPNS name
   197→    - If found: restore to that folder
   198→    - If NOT found: the parent was also deleted or moved
   199→      -> Check if parent is also in the bin
   200→      -> If parent in bin: recreate the folder path first (recursive restore)
   201→      -> If parent truly gone: restore to root folder
   202→  |
   203→  v
   204→[2] Add the preserved FolderChild back to the target folder's children
   205→    - For files: re-insert the FilePointer into parent's children array
   206→    - For folders: re-insert the FolderEntry into parent's children array
   207→    - Check for name collisions (append " (restored)" suffix if needed)
   208→  |
   209→  v
   210→[3] Publish updated parent folder metadata (IPNS)
   211→  |
   212→  v
   213→[4] Remove BinEntry from RecycleBinMetadata
   214→    Publish updated bin IPNS record
   215→  |
   216→  v
   217→[5] Update local stores:
   218→    - folderStore: add item back to parent children
   219→    - binStore: remove bin entry
   220→```
   221→
   222→### Permanent Delete Flow
   223→
   224→```
   225→User clicks "Delete permanently" or auto-purge triggers
   226→  |
   227→  v
   228→[1] For files:
   229→    - Resolve file's IPNS name -> get FileMetadata -> get CID(s)
   230→    - Unpin all CIDs (current version + past versions if any)
   231→    - Update quota (removeUsage)
   232→    - (TEE unenrollment deferred -- records expire naturally)
   233→  |
   234→  v
   235→[1b] For folders:
   236→    - Recursively resolve folder IPNS -> get all descendant file CIDs
   237→    - Unpin all CIDs
   238→    - Update quota
   239→  |
   240→  v
   241→[2] Remove BinEntry from RecycleBinMetadata
   242→    Publish updated bin IPNS record
   243→  |
   244→  v
   245→[3] Update local stores:
   246→    - binStore: remove entry
   247→    - quotaStore: adjust used bytes
   248→```
   249→
   250→### Auto-Purge Flow (Client-Side)
   251→
   252→```
   253→On app load OR when user navigates to /bin:
   254→  |
   255→  v
   256→[1] Load RecycleBinMetadata from IPNS
   257→  |
   258→  v
   259→[2] Filter entries where (now - deletedAt) > retentionPeriodMs
   260→  |
   261→  v
   262→[3] For each expired entry: execute permanent delete flow
   263→  |
   264→  v
   265→[4] Publish updated bin metadata (batch - single IPNS publish)
   266→```
   267→
   268→**Important**: Auto-purge is client-side only. If the user never opens the app, items remain in the bin past the retention period but are purged next time the client loads. This is acceptable because:
   269→
   270→- Storage quota still counts bin items (no free ride by not opening the app)
   271→- The retention period is a UX guideline, not a strict SLA
   272→- Server-side purge would require the server to decrypt bin metadata, violating zero-knowledge
   273→
   274→### Desktop FUSE Integration
   275→
   276→Current `handle_unlink` and `handle_rmdir` in `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/fuse/write_ops.rs`:
   277→
   278→1. Remove inode from local tree
   279→2. Update folder metadata (publish to IPNS)
   280→3. Fire-and-forget unpin of CID
   281→
   282→**Change**: Instead of unpinning in step 3, send a message to the webview to execute the soft-delete bin service call. The webview has the user's keys and can encrypt/publish the bin metadata.
   283→
   284→```
   285→Current FUSE unlink:
   286→  remove inode -> update folder IPNS -> unpin CID (fire-and-forget)
   287→
   288→New FUSE unlink:
   289→  remove inode -> update folder IPNS -> IPC to webview: "addToBin(item)"
   290→```
   291→
   292→The Rust side already sends metadata to the webview for IPNS publishing via `update_folder_metadata()`. The bin entry creation requires the user's ECIES public key for bin metadata encryption. This key is available in the webview's auth store. So the bin metadata publish must happen on the webview side.
   293→
   294→**Minimal approach**: The Rust `handle_unlink`/`handle_rmdir` already correctly removes the child from folder metadata and publishes. The only change needed is: instead of calling `unpin_content()`, emit a Tauri event or invoke a webview JS function that calls the bin service to add the entry. The item data (FilePointer/FolderEntry) needs to be captured before removal and passed to the webview.
   295→
   296→### Sync Across Devices
   297→
   298→The bin IPNS record is included in the same IPNS polling mechanism as folder metadata:
   299→
   300→- TEE republishes the bin IPNS record every 3 hours (enrolled on first bin write)
   301→- Client polls every 30s, compares bin IPNS CID
   302→- On change, re-fetches and decrypts bin metadata
   303→- Local bin store is updated
   304→
   305→**Conflict handling**: The bin metadata uses a `sequenceNumber` (same as DeviceRegistry). On concurrent modification, the conflict detection from Phase 16 applies. Use optimistic concurrency: if sequence mismatch on publish, re-read remote, merge entries, retry.
   306→
   307→**Merge strategy for bin entries**: Additive merge (union of entries). If both devices deleted different items simultaneously, the merged bin has both. If the same item appears in both (same bin entry ID), keep the one with the earlier `deletedAt` (or either -- they are identical since the same item was deleted).
   308→
   309→## Don't Hand-Roll
   310→
   311→| Problem                     | Don't Build           | Use Instead                                                                           | Why                                                              |
   312→| --------------------------- | --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
   313→| IPNS key derivation for bin | Custom key generation | HKDF with `cipherbox-recycle-bin-ipns-v1` info string, same pattern as vault/registry | Domain-separated, deterministic, established pattern             |
   314→| Bin metadata encryption     | Custom scheme         | ECIES with user's publicKey (same as DeviceRegistry)                                  | Zero-knowledge, user-scoped, no symmetric key to manage          |
   315→| Flat list UI                | Custom file browser   | Adapt existing `FileListItem` component pattern                                       | Consistent UX, reuse selection/context menu logic                |
   316→| Confirmation dialogs        | New dialog component  | Existing `ConfirmDialog` component                                                    | Already supports destructive styling, loading state              |
   317→| Multi-select                | Custom selection      | Existing `SelectionActionBar` pattern from FileBrowser                                | Consistent interaction, already supports batch operations        |
   318→| Auto-purge scheduling       | Server-side cron      | Client-side check on load/navigate                                                    | Zero-knowledge constraint -- server cannot read bin metadata     |
   319→| Environment config          | Hardcoded values      | NestJS `ConfigService` with `RECYCLE_BIN_RETENTION_DAYS`                              | Follows existing pattern (Redis, DB, CORS all use ConfigService) |
   320→
   321→**Key insight:** Every infrastructure piece needed for the recycle bin already exists in CipherBox. The bin is essentially a "special folder" with ECIES encryption (like device registry) instead of AES-GCM encryption (like regular folders), plus business logic for retention and restore.
   322→
   323→## Common Pitfalls
   324→
   325→### Pitfall 1: Orphaned IPNS Records Accumulating
   326→
   327→**What goes wrong:** Every deleted item's IPNS record remains enrolled in TEE republishing. If a user deletes hundreds of files and never permanently deletes them, the TEE republish queue grows indefinitely.
   328→**Why it happens:** Soft-delete intentionally keeps IPNS records alive for restore.
   329→**How to avoid:** On permanent delete, add TEE unenrollment (if an API endpoint exists by then -- currently deferred to "Phase 14 TODO"). At minimum, document this as a known limitation. The republish service already has capacity warnings at 1000+ records.
   330→**Warning signs:** TEE republish queue depth metric growing without plateau.
   331→
   332→### Pitfall 2: Bin Metadata Blob Size Growth
   333→
   334→**What goes wrong:** If a user deletes hundreds of items, each BinEntry contains a full FolderEntry or FilePointer. The bin metadata blob grows, increasing IPFS upload/download time.
   335→**Why it happens:** Each BinEntry preserves the full FolderChild for restore.
   336→**How to avoid:**
   337→
   338→- Auto-purge on load keeps the bin bounded by retention period
   339→- A 30-day retention with typical usage (say 100 items deleted per month) results in ~50KB of bin metadata. This is well within acceptable limits.
   340→- Add a safety check: if bin metadata exceeds 1MB, warn the user and suggest emptying the bin.
   341→  **Warning signs:** Bin load time > 2s.
   342→
   343→### Pitfall 3: Stale `originalParentIpnsName` After Folder Moves
   344→
   345→**What goes wrong:** User deletes a file from folder A, then moves folder A to a different location. The bin entry's `originalParentIpnsName` still points to folder A's IPNS name, which is correct (IPNS names don't change on move). But the `originalPath` display string is now inaccurate.
   346→**Why it happens:** The display path is captured at deletion time.
   347→**How to avoid:** Accept that `originalPath` is "path at deletion time" -- display it with a note "(at time of deletion)". The IPNS-based restore logic will correctly find the moved folder regardless of its current location in the tree.
   348→**Warning signs:** User confusion when displayed path doesn't match current folder structure.
   349→
   350→### Pitfall 4: Concurrent Delete-and-Restore Race
   351→
   352→**What goes wrong:** On device A, user deletes a file. On device B (before sync), user tries to access the same file. After sync, device B sees the file is gone.
   353→**Why it happens:** IPNS polling is 30s. Within that window, the two devices have divergent state.
   354→**How to avoid:** This is the same eventual consistency the app already handles for all operations. The sync mechanism (Phase 16) already handles concurrent modifications. The bin just adds a recovery path -- the user can restore the file from the bin on any device.
   355→**Warning signs:** None specific -- this is inherent to eventual consistency.
   356→
   357→### Pitfall 5: Deleting Shared Items
   358→
   359→**What goes wrong:** User deletes a file that is actively shared with another user. The file goes to the owner's bin, but the recipient loses access.
   360→**Why it happens:** The share references the item by IPNS name. When removed from the folder, the share's reference becomes dangling.
   361→**How to avoid:** For v1, accept this behavior -- the owner's delete takes precedence. The shared user will see a resolution error for that IPNS name. Future enhancement: notify shared users when a shared item is deleted.
   362→**Warning signs:** Share recipients see "file not found" errors.
   363→
   364→### Pitfall 6: Restoring to a Deleted Parent Folder
   365→
   366→**What goes wrong:** User deletes folder A (which contained file B), then tries to restore file B. The original parent (folder A) no longer exists in the folder tree.
   367→**Why it happens:** File B's `originalParentIpnsName` points to folder A, which is itself in the bin.
   368→**How to avoid:** Implement the "recreate path" logic from CONTEXT.md:
   369→
   370→1. Look up `originalParentIpnsName` in the folder tree
   371→2. If not found, check if a bin entry exists with a matching IPNS name
   372→3. If parent is in bin, restore the parent first (recursively)
   373→4. If parent is nowhere (permanently deleted), restore to root
   374→   This must be clearly implemented with recursion guards (max depth) to prevent infinite loops.
   375→   **Warning signs:** "Folder not found" errors during restore.
   376→
   377→### Pitfall 7: Size Calculation for Folder Bin Entries
   378→
   379→**What goes wrong:** When deleting a folder, its `size` for quota display and purge-time unpin requires resolving all descendant file metadata IPNS records. This is expensive.
   380→**Why it happens:** Folder metadata only contains FilePointers (no inline size), and the folder tree may have deep nesting.
   381→**How to avoid:**
   382→
   383→- On delete: if the folder's subtree is loaded in the folder store, calculate size from loaded data. If not fully loaded, use 0 as size and display "Unknown" in the bin.
   384→- On permanent delete: resolve the full subtree to unpin all CIDs. This is inherently async and can be done in background.
   385→- Accept that folder size in the bin view may be approximate or unknown.
   386→  **Warning signs:** Long delays during folder deletion if trying to resolve all descendant sizes eagerly.
   387→
   388→## Code Examples
   389→
   390→### Bin IPNS Key Derivation (follows registry pattern exactly)
   391→
   392→```typescript
   393→// Source: modeled on packages/crypto/src/registry/derive-ipns.ts
   394→const BIN_HKDF_SALT = new TextEncoder().encode('CipherBox-v1');
   395→const BIN_HKDF_INFO = new TextEncoder().encode('cipherbox-recycle-bin-ipns-v1');
   396→
   397→export async function deriveBinIpnsKeypair(userPrivateKey: Uint8Array): Promise<{
   398→  privateKey: Uint8Array;
   399→  publicKey: Uint8Array;
   400→  ipnsName: string;
   401→}> {
   402→  if (userPrivateKey.length !== SECP256K1_PRIVATE_KEY_SIZE) {
   403→    throw new CryptoError('Invalid private key size for bin derivation', 'INVALID_KEY_SIZE');
   404→  }
   405→
   406→  const ed25519Seed = await deriveKey({
   407→    inputKey: userPrivateKey,
   408→    salt: BIN_HKDF_SALT,

   420→### Bin Metadata Encryption/Decryption (follows registry pattern)

   422→```typescript

   424→export async function encryptBinMetadata(
   425→  metadata: RecycleBinMetadata,
   426→  userPublicKey: Uint8Array
   427→): Promise<Uint8Array> {
   428→  const json = JSON.stringify(metadata);
   429→  const plaintext = new TextEncoder().encode(json);
   430→  return wrapKey(plaintext, userPublicKey); // ECIES encrypt

   433→export async function decryptBinMetadata(
   434→  ciphertext: Uint8Array,
   435→  userPrivateKey: Uint8Array

   544→## Open Questions
   545→
   546→1. **ECIES max plaintext size for bin metadata**
   547→   - What we know: DeviceRegistry uses ECIES for the entire blob. The eciesjs library uses AES-256-GCM internally for the payload, so there's no practical size limit.
   548→   - What's unclear: Performance with very large bin metadata (1000+ entries). Each entry is ~500 bytes, so 1000 entries = ~500KB ECIES payload.
   549→   - Recommendation: Test with 1000 entries during implementation. Add a safety cap (e.g., 5000 entries max) with a warning to empty the bin.
   550→
   551→2. **TEE enrollment for the bin IPNS record**
   552→   - What we know: TEE republishing keeps IPNS records alive. The bin IPNS record needs to be enrolled (same as vault, device registry, all folder IPNS records).
   553→   - What's unclear: The bin IPNS key is derived via HKDF, not randomly generated. Is the TEE enrollment path the same? (Answer: yes, the TEE receives the encrypted IPNS private key regardless of derivation method.)
   554→   - Recommendation: Enroll the bin IPNS key with TEE on first bin write, same as vault/registry IPNS enrollment.
   555→
   556→3. **Folder size in bin entries**
   557→   - What we know: Files have `size` in their FileMetadata. Folders don't have a single size -- need to sum all descendant files.
   558→   - What's unclear: How to handle partially-loaded folder trees (not all subfolders are loaded in memory).
   559→   - Recommendation: For files, use the known size from FileMetadata (resolved at delete time if possible). For folders, store 0 and display "Folder" without size. Size is only critical for quota (which is tracked server-side via pins anyway).
   560→
   561→4. **Batch operations and IPNS publish count**
   562→   - What we know: Deleting multiple items from the same folder = 1 folder IPNS publish + 1 bin IPNS publish.
   563→   - What's unclear: With optimistic concurrency, if the bin publish conflicts, the folder publish already succeeded. Need atomic-like behavior.
   564→   - Recommendation: Use add-before-remove pattern: write to bin first, then remove from folder. If bin publish fails, items stay in both places (recoverable). On next load, detect duplicates and reconcile.

1→//! HKDF-SHA256 deterministic IPNS keypair derivation.
     2→//!
     3→//! Derives deterministic Ed25519 IPNS keypairs from a secp256k1 private key
     4→//! using HKDF-SHA256 with domain-separated info strings. Matches the TypeScript
     5→//! implementations in `@cipherbox/crypto` (vault/derive-ipns.ts, file/derive-ipns.ts,
     6→//! registry/derive-ipns.ts).
     7→//!
     8→//! Derivation path:
     9→//!   secp256k1 privateKey (32 bytes)
    10→//!     -> HKDF-SHA256(salt="CipherBox-v1", info=<domain-specific>)
    11→//!     -> 32-byte Ed25519 seed
    12→//!     -> Ed25519 keypair
    13→//!     -> IPNS name (k51...)
    14→
    15→use ed25519_dalek::SigningKey;
    16→use hkdf::Hkdf;
    17→use sha2::Sha256;
    18→use thiserror::Error;
    19→use zeroize::{Zeroize, Zeroizing};
    20→
    21→use super::ipns;
    22→
    23→/// Common HKDF salt for all CipherBox derivations.
    24→const HKDF_SALT: &[u8] = b"CipherBox-v1";
    25→
    26→/// HKDF info for vault IPNS keypair derivation.
    27→const VAULT_HKDF_INFO: &[u8] = b"cipherbox-vault-ipns-v1";
    28→
    29→/// HKDF info for device registry IPNS keypair derivation.
    30→const REGISTRY_HKDF_INFO: &[u8] = b"cipherbox-device-registry-ipns-v1";
    31→
    32→/// HKDF info prefix for per-file IPNS keypair derivation.
    33→const FILE_HKDF_INFO_PREFIX: &str = "cipherbox-file-ipns-v1:";
    34→
    35→/// Minimum file ID length (matches TypeScript validation).
    36→const MIN_FILE_ID_LENGTH: usize = 10;
    37→
    38→#[derive(Debug, Error)]
    39→pub enum HkdfError {
    40→    #[error("Invalid key size")]
    41→    InvalidKeySize,
    42→    #[error("HKDF derivation failed")]
    43→    DerivationFailed,
    44→    #[error("IPNS name derivation failed")]
    45→    IpnsDerivationFailed,
    46→    #[error("Invalid file ID: must be at least {MIN_FILE_ID_LENGTH} characters")]
    47→    InvalidFileId,
    48→}
    49→
    50→/// Internal helper: derive an Ed25519 keypair and IPNS name from HKDF output.
    51→///
    52→/// All three public functions follow the same pattern and delegate here.
    53→fn derive_ipns_keypair(
    54→    user_private_key: &[u8; 32],
    55→    info: &[u8],
    56→) -> Result<(Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>, Vec<u8>, String), HkdfError> {
    57→    // 1. HKDF-SHA256: extract + expand
    58→    let hk = Hkdf::<Sha256>::new(Some(HKDF_SALT), user_private_key);
    59→    let mut okm = [0u8; 32];
    60→    hk.expand(info, &mut okm)
    61→        .map_err(|_| HkdfError::DerivationFailed)?;
    62→
    63→    // 2. Ed25519 keypair from 32-byte seed
    64→    let signing_key = SigningKey::from_bytes(&okm);
    65→    okm.zeroize();
    66→    let verifying_key = signing_key.verifying_key();
    67→
    68→    let private_key = Zeroizing::new(signing_key.to_bytes().to_vec());
    69→    let public_key = verifying_key.to_bytes().to_vec();
    70→
    71→    // 3. Derive IPNS name from public key
    72→    let pk_array: [u8; 32] = verifying_key.to_bytes();
    73→    let ipns_name = ipns::derive_ipns_name(&pk_array).map_err(|_| HkdfError::IpnsDerivationFailed)?;
    74→
    75→    Ok((private_key, public_key, ipns_name))
    76→}
    77→
    78→/// Derive the deterministic Ed25519 IPNS keypair for the user's vault.
    79→///
    80→/// Uses HKDF info "cipherbox-vault-ipns-v1" for domain separation.
    81→///
    82→/// Given the same secp256k1 privateKey, this always produces the same
    83→/// IPNS name, enabling vault discovery from any device with the user's key.
    84→///
    85→/// Returns (ed25519_private_key, ed25519_public_key, ipns_name).
    86→pub fn derive_vault_ipns_keypair(
    87→    user_private_key: &[u8; 32],
    88→) -> Result<(Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>, Vec<u8>, String), HkdfError> {
    89→    derive_ipns_keypair(user_private_key, VAULT_HKDF_INFO)
    90→}
    91→
    92→/// Derive a deterministic Ed25519 IPNS keypair for a specific file.
    93→///
    94→/// Uses HKDF info "cipherbox-file-ipns-v1:{fileId}" for per-file domain separation.
    95→///
    96→/// Returns (ed25519_private_key, ed25519_public_key, ipns_name).
    97→pub fn derive_file_ipns_keypair(
    98→    user_private_key: &[u8; 32],
    99→    file_id: &str,
   100→) -> Result<(Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>, Vec<u8>, String), HkdfError> {
   101→    if file_id.len() < MIN_FILE_ID_LENGTH {
   102→        return Err(HkdfError::InvalidFileId);
   103→    }
   104→
   105→    let info = format!("{}{}", FILE_HKDF_INFO_PREFIX, file_id);
   106→    derive_ipns_keypair(user_private_key, info.as_bytes())
   107→}
   108→
   109→/// Derive the deterministic Ed25519 IPNS keypair for the device registry.
   110→///
   111→/// Uses HKDF info "cipherbox-device-registry-ipns-v1" for domain separation.
   112→///
   113→/// Returns (ed25519_private_key, ed25519_public_key, ipns_name).
   114→pub fn derive_registry_ipns_keypair(
   115→    user_private_key: &[u8; 32],
   116→) -> Result<(Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>, Vec<u8>, String), HkdfError> {
   117→    derive_ipns_keypair(user_private_key, REGISTRY_HKDF_INFO)
   118→}

    81→/// Decrypted folder metadata structure (v2 schema with per-file IPNS pointers).
    82→/// The entire FolderMetadata object is encrypted as a single blob with AES-256-GCM.
    83→/// Children can be FolderEntry (subfolder) or FilePointer (slim IPNS reference).
    84→#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    85→pub struct FolderMetadata {
    86→    /// Schema version (always "v2").
    87→    pub version: String,
    88→    /// Folders and file pointers in this folder.
    89→    pub children: Vec<FolderChild>,
    90→}
    91→
    92→/// Encrypt folder metadata with AES-256-GCM.
    93→///
    94→/// JSON serializes the metadata, then seals with AES-GCM.
    95→/// Returns the sealed bytes: IV (12) || ciphertext || tag (16).
    96→pub fn encrypt_folder_metadata(
    97→    metadata: &FolderMetadata,
    98→    folder_key: &[u8; 32],
    99→) -> Result<Vec<u8>, FolderError> {
   100→    let mut json = serde_json::to_vec(metadata).map_err(|_| FolderError::SerializationFailed)?;
   101→    let result = aes::seal_aes_gcm(&json, folder_key).map_err(FolderError::EncryptionFailed);
   102→    json.zeroize();
   103→    result
   104→}
   105→
   106→/// Decrypt folder metadata from AES-256-GCM sealed bytes.
   107→///
   108→/// Unseals, then JSON deserializes to FolderMetadata.
   109→/// Rejects metadata with version other than "v2".
   110→pub fn decrypt_folder_metadata(
   111→    sealed: &[u8],
   112→    folder_key: &[u8; 32],
   113→) -> Result<FolderMetadata, FolderError> {
   114→    let mut json = aes::unseal_aes_gcm(sealed, folder_key).map_err(FolderError::EncryptionFailed)?;
   115→
   116→    // Parse as generic JSON to check version field
   117→    let value: serde_json::Value =
   118→        serde_json::from_slice(&json).map_err(|e| {
   119→            log::error!("JSON parse failed: {}", e);
   120→            json.zeroize();
   121→            FolderError::DeserializationFailed
   122→        })?;
   123→
   124→    let version = value.get("version").and_then(|v| v.as_str());
   125→    if version != Some("v2") {
   126→        log::error!(
   127→            "Unsupported folder metadata version: {:?} (only v2 is supported)",
   128→            version
   129→        );
   130→        json.zeroize();
   131→        return Err(FolderError::DeserializationFailed);
   132→    }
   133→
   134→    let result: Result<FolderMetadata, _> = serde_json::from_value(value).map_err(|e| {
   135→        log::error!("V2 metadata deserialization failed: {}", e);
   136→        FolderError::DeserializationFailed
   137→    });
   138→
   139→    json.zeroize();
   140→    result
   141→}
   142→
   143→/// Default encryption mode for FileMetadata: "GCM".
   144→fn default_encryption_mode() -> String {
   145→    "GCM".to_string()
   146→}
   147→
   148→/// A single past version of a file.
   149→/// Stores full crypto context for independent decryption.
   150→/// Matches TypeScript `VersionEntry` from `@cipherbox/crypto/file/types.ts`.
   151→#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
   152→#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
   153→pub struct VersionEntry {
   154→    /// IPFS CID of the encrypted file content for this version.
   155→    pub cid: String,
   156→    /// Hex-encoded ECIES-wrapped AES-256 key for decrypting this version.
   157→    pub file_key_encrypted: String,
   158→    /// Hex-encoded IV used for this version's encryption.
   159→    pub file_iv: String,
   160→    /// Original file size in bytes (before encryption).
   161→    pub size: u64,
   162→    /// When this version was created (Unix ms).
   163→    pub timestamp: u64,
   164→    /// Encryption mode used for this version.
   165→    pub encryption_mode: String,
   166→}
   167→
   168→/// Decrypted per-file metadata structure.
   169→/// Stored as an encrypted blob in the file's own IPNS record.
   170→/// Encrypted with the parent folder's folderKey (NOT the file's own key).
   171→/// Matches TypeScript `FileMetadata` from `@cipherbox/crypto/file/types.ts`.
   172→#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
   173→#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
   174→pub struct FileMetadata {
   175→    /// Schema version.
   176→    pub version: String,
   177→    /// IPFS CID of the encrypted file content.
   178→    pub cid: String,
   179→    /// Hex-encoded ECIES-wrapped AES-256 key for decrypting file.
   180→    pub file_key_encrypted: String,
   181→    /// Hex-encoded IV used for file encryption.
   182→    pub file_iv: String,
   183→    /// Original file size in bytes (before encryption).
   184→    pub size: u64,
   185→    /// MIME type of the original file.
   186→    pub mime_type: String,
   187→    /// Encryption mode (optional for backward compat; defaults to "GCM").
   188→    #[serde(default = "default_encryption_mode")]
   189→    pub encryption_mode: String,
   190→    /// Creation timestamp (Unix ms).
   191→    pub created_at: u64,
   192→    /// Last modification timestamp (Unix ms).
   193→    pub modified_at: u64,
   194→    /// Past versions of this file (newest first). None if no versions exist.
   195→    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
   196→    #[serde(default)]
   197→    pub versions: Option<Vec<VersionEntry>>,
   198→}
   199→
   200→/// Encrypt file metadata with AES-256-GCM.
   201→///
   202→/// JSON serializes the metadata, then seals with AES-GCM.
   203→/// Uses the parent folder's folderKey for encryption.
   204→/// Returns the sealed bytes: IV (12) || ciphertext || tag (16).
   205→pub fn encrypt_file_metadata(
   206→    metadata: &FileMetadata,
   207→    folder_key: &[u8; 32],
   208→) -> Result<Vec<u8>, FolderError> {
   209→    let mut json = serde_json::to_vec(metadata).map_err(|_| FolderError::SerializationFailed)?;
   210→    let result = aes::seal_aes_gcm(&json, folder_key).map_err(FolderError::EncryptionFailed);
   211→    json.zeroize();
   212→    result
   213→}
   214→
   215→/// Decrypt file metadata from AES-256-GCM sealed bytes.
   216→///
   217→/// Uses the parent folder's folderKey for decryption.
   218→/// Unseals, then JSON deserializes to FileMetadata.
   219→pub fn decrypt_file_metadata(
   220→    sealed: &[u8],
   221→    folder_key: &[u8; 32],
   222→) -> Result<FileMetadata, FolderError> {
   223→    let mut json = aes::unseal_aes_gcm(sealed, folder_key).map_err(FolderError::EncryptionFailed)?;
   224→    let result = serde_json::from_slice(&json).map_err(|_| FolderError::DeserializationFailed);
   225→    json.zeroize();
   226→    result
   227→}
   228→

    86→# ---- Summary ----

    88→echo "  Summary"
    89→echo "============================================"
    90→echo "  Total failures: $TOTAL_FAIL"

1→#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2→set -uo pipefail
     3→
     4→# test-fuse-operations.sh -- Exercise FUSE mount file I/O operations.
     5→#
     6→# Usage: ./test-fuse-operations.sh [mount-point]
     7→#   mount-point  Path to FUSE mount (default: $HOME/CipherBox)
     8→#
     9→# Tests: create, read, overwrite, mkdir, nested write, binary round-trip,
    10→#        rename, delete file, delete directory.
    11→#
    12→# Exit code: number of failed tests (0 = all passed).
    13→
    14→MP="${1:-$HOME/CipherBox}"
    15→PASS=0
    16→FAIL=0
    17→
    18→# Detect SHA-256 command (macOS vs Linux)
    19→if command -v shasum &>/dev/null; then
    20→  SHA256_CMD="shasum -a 256"
    21→elif command -v sha256sum &>/dev/null; then
    22→  SHA256_CMD="sha256sum"
    23→else
    24→  echo "FAIL: No SHA-256 command found (shasum or sha256sum)"
    25→  exit 1
    26→fi
    27→
    28→pass() {
    29→  PASS=$((PASS + 1))
    30→  echo "PASS: $1"
    31→}
    32→
    33→fail() {
    34→  FAIL=$((FAIL + 1))
    35→  echo "FAIL: $1"
    36→}
    37→
    38→echo "=== FUSE File I/O Tests ==="
    39→echo "Mount point: $MP"
    40→echo ""
    41→
    42→# ---- Test 1: Create and read text file ----
    43→echo "--- Test 1: Create and read text file ---"
    44→echo "Hello from CI" > "$MP/e2e-test.txt"
    45→sleep 3
    46→CONTENT=$(cat "$MP/e2e-test.txt")
    47→if [ "$CONTENT" = "Hello from CI" ]; then
    48→  pass "Create and read text file"
    49→else
    50→  fail "Create and read text file (got: '$CONTENT')"
    51→fi
    52→
    53→# ---- Test 2: Create directory ----
    54→echo "--- Test 2: Create directory ---"
    55→mkdir -p "$MP/e2e-folder"
    56→if [ -d "$MP/e2e-folder" ]; then
    57→  pass "Create directory"
    58→else
    59→  fail "Create directory"
    60→fi
    61→
    62→# ---- Test 3: Write file in subdirectory ----
    63→echo "--- Test 3: Write file in subdirectory ---"
    64→echo "Nested content" > "$MP/e2e-folder/nested.txt"
    65→sleep 3
    66→NESTED=$(cat "$MP/e2e-folder/nested.txt")
    67→if [ "$NESTED" = "Nested content" ]; then
    68→  pass "Write file in subdirectory"
    69→else
    70→  fail "Write file in subdirectory (got: '$NESTED')"
    71→fi
    72→
    73→# ---- Test 4: Overwrite file (modify) ----
    74→echo "--- Test 4: Overwrite file ---"
    75→echo "Modified content" > "$MP/e2e-test.txt"
    76→sleep 3
    77→MODIFIED=$(cat "$MP/e2e-test.txt")
    78→if [ "$MODIFIED" = "Modified content" ]; then
    79→  pass "Overwrite file"
    80→else
    81→  fail "Overwrite file (got: '$MODIFIED')"
    82→fi
    83→
    84→# ---- Test 5: Binary file round-trip ----
    85→echo "--- Test 5: Binary file round-trip ---"
    86→dd if=/dev/urandom of=/tmp/e2e-binary.bin bs=1024 count=256 2>/dev/null
    87→cp /tmp/e2e-binary.bin "$MP/e2e-binary.bin"
    88→sleep 5
    89→CHECKSUM_ORIG=$($SHA256_CMD /tmp/e2e-binary.bin | cut -d' ' -f1)
    90→CHECKSUM_MOUNT=$($SHA256_CMD "$MP/e2e-binary.bin" | cut -d' ' -f1)
    91→if [ "$CHECKSUM_ORIG" = "$CHECKSUM_MOUNT" ]; then
    92→  pass "Binary file round-trip (256KB)"
    93→else
    94→  fail "Binary file round-trip (orig: $CHECKSUM_ORIG, mount: $CHECKSUM_MOUNT)"
    95→fi
    96→
    97→# ---- Test 6: Rename file ----
    98→echo "--- Test 6: Rename file ---"
    99→mv "$MP/e2e-test.txt" "$MP/e2e-renamed.txt"
   100→sleep 2
   101→if [ ! -f "$MP/e2e-test.txt" ] && [ -f "$MP/e2e-renamed.txt" ]; then
   102→  RENAMED=$(cat "$MP/e2e-renamed.txt")
   103→  if [ "$RENAMED" = "Modified content" ]; then
   104→    pass "Rename file"
   105→  else
   106→    fail "Rename file (content changed: '$RENAMED')"
   107→  fi
   108→else
   109→  fail "Rename file (old exists: $(test -f "$MP/e2e-test.txt" && echo yes || echo no), new exists: $(test -f "$MP/e2e-renamed.txt" && echo yes || echo no))"
   110→fi
   111→
   112→# ---- Test 7: Delete file ----
   113→echo "--- Test 7: Delete file ---"
   114→rm "$MP/e2e-renamed.txt"
   115→sleep 2
   116→if [ ! -f "$MP/e2e-renamed.txt" ]; then
   117→  pass "Delete file"
   118→else
   119→  fail "Delete file (still exists)"
   120→fi
   121→
   122→# ---- Test 8: Delete directory ----
   123→echo "--- Test 8: Delete directory ---"
   124→rm -rf "$MP/e2e-folder"
   125→sleep 2
   126→if [ ! -d "$MP/e2e-folder" ]; then
   127→  pass "Delete directory"
   128→else
   129→  fail "Delete directory (still exists)"
   130→fi
   131→
   132→# ---- Test 9: Cleanup ----
   133→echo "--- Test 9: Cleanup ---"
   134→rm -f "$MP/e2e-binary.bin" 2>/dev/null || true
   135→rm -f /tmp/e2e-binary.bin 2>/dev/null || true
   136→# Filter .DS_Store from any remaining file checks
   137→REMAINING=$(ls "$MP" 2>/dev/null | grep -v '\.DS_Store' | grep -v '^$' || true)
   138→if [ -z "$REMAINING" ]; then
   139→  pass "Cleanup (mount point clean)"
   140→else
   141→  # Not a hard failure -- other files may be present from the desktop app
   142→  pass "Cleanup (remaining files: $REMAINING)"
   143→fi
   144→
   145→# ---- Summary ----
   146→echo ""
   147→echo "=== FUSE File I/O Results ==="
   148→echo "  Passed: $PASS"
   149→echo "  Failed: $FAIL"
   150→echo "=============================="
   151→
   152→exit "$FAIL"
   153→
